opmerking: Openheid gelezen op de eigen Engelse sites (alleen pagina's die via zoeken gevonden en opgehaald konden worden), risico's uit één nieuwszoekactie per kliniek in Engels en Koreaans. Geen enkele kliniek publiceert vaste operatieprijzen; View geeft alleen een geschat bereik, Braun alleen medicijnkosten. Geen enkele kliniek heeft een schriftelijk revisie- of garantiebeleid gevonden (JW heeft wel een terugbetalingsregeling voor de aanbetaling). De meeste ernstige zaken in de pers (sterfgevallen, ghost surgery) noemen de kliniek niet; die staan onder algemeen en zijn niet aan een kliniek gekoppeld. 'Geen risico gevonden' betekent: niets gevonden in één zoekactie, niet: bewezen schoon. Voor 15 kandidaten kon geen eigen Engelse site worden gecontroleerd.

algemeen.wat: Since 25 September 2023 the amended Medical Service Act requires CCTV in every operating room where patients are under general anaesthesia; surgeons may only refuse recording for valid reasons, footage is viewable on request of investigators, a court or with consent of patient and staff, and leaking or falsifying footage carries up to 5 years in prison or a 50 million won fine.

In 2025 a record 2.01 million foreign patients from 201 countries were treated in Korea (1.17 million in 2024); 62.9% of visits were dermatology and 11.2% plastic surgery; 87.2% of care was in Seoul (Ministry of Health and Welfare).
Ministry figures for 2025: China 30.8%, Japan 29.8%, Taiwan 9.2% and the US 8.6% of foreign patients; US patients rose 70.4% to 173,000.
In 2023, 605,768 foreign patients were treated, 16.8% of them for plastic surgery; reports of illegal patient solicitation to KHIDI rose from 11 (2021) to 59 (2023), with little visible follow-up.

Under the 2016 act on attracting foreign patients, recruiting agencies and clinics must register; unregistered brokers face up to 3 years in prison or a 30 million won fine, and clinics treating foreign patients need malpractice insurance.

KHIDI guidelines bar unregistered hospitals from counselling or booking foreign patients online, including via foreign social media accounts; violations carry up to 3 years in prison or 30 million won.

The 10% VAT refund for foreign patients on cosmetic surgery and dermatology ended on 31 December 2025; experts warned this may weaken price transparency and revive illegal brokers. Refunds reached 95.5 billion won in 2024.

The Korea Consumer Agency received 4,816 plastic surgery complaints in 2013 and ruled for damages in 214 cases over two years; 80.9% of Seoul cases involved Gangnam, and only five cases were filed by foreigners.
A National Forensic Service study counted 50 deaths related to cosmetic procedures from 2016 to 2024 (about 5.6 per year), rising over the period.

A Chinese woman in her 20s died in January 2024 after three liposuction sessions at an unnamed Gangnam clinic; prosecutors indicted the clinic director for professional negligence resulting in death in June 2026. He was already on trial over a 2018 death of another Chinese patient after liposuction.
After that death the Chinese embassy in Seoul warned its citizens about cosmetic surgery risks in Korea and advised checking brokers, clinics and surgeons.

A Seoul civil court ordered a surgeon at an unnamed Gangnam clinic to pay about 200 million won to the parents of a Chinese teenager who died after an 11-hour liposuction and fat-transfer operation in 2018, finding vital signs were not monitored; she had been referred by an agency.

In the 2016 death of student Kwon Dae-hee after facial contouring surgery (a ghost surgery case), the clinic director was sentenced at first instance to 3 years in prison; the court found treatment and transfer were delayed while he lost blood.

Prosecutors indicted a Sinsa-dong clinic operator for having a dentist perform surgeries under anaesthesia while a plastic surgeon did the consultations (33 patients, about 152 million won), after an 18-year-old patient died in 2014.

In the 2020 liposuction death of Hong Kong heiress Bonnie Evita Law, reportedly introduced by an illegal broker, the surgeon was acquitted of negligent homicide at first instance but fined 3 million won for attracting foreign patients without registration.

Seoul's special judicial police found 36 medical waste violations at 25 plastic surgery and dermatology clinics, including liposuction fat and blood poured down sinks, and referred 25 people to prosecutors.
Korea Customs Service alleged a 102 million dollar crypto laundering network around payments by Chinese patients at an unnamed large plastic surgery clinic; three people were referred to prosecutors.

The Supreme Court upheld a one-year prison sentence for a lawyer who published a secret operating room recording alleging ghost surgery at an unnamed Gangnam clinic; the courts did not find that ghost surgery occurred.
The Fair Trade Commission sanctioned View, DA and AB Plastic Surgery for undisclosed paid reviews and passed suspected Medical Service Act violations to the Ministry of Health and Welfare.
